title: Check your understanding: Removing Sensitive Data from History

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of removing sensitive data from history?
options: History rewriting can remove sensitive content from reachable history in a carefully controlled process, but it cannot guarantee deletion from every clone, cache or backup. Credential rotation and incident response remain essential.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: History rewriting can remove sensitive content from reachable history in a carefully controlled process, but it cannot guarantee deletion from every clone, cache or backup. Credential rotation and incident response remain essential.
questions.explanation: History rewriting can remove sensitive content from reachable history in a carefully controlled process, but it cannot guarantee deletion from every clone, cache or backup. Credential rotation and incident response remain essential.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git log --all -- path/to/secret.txt` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with removing sensitive data from history?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
